extensions.scope: Vizion Motor surface only (pi/motor_monitor/web/). The root DESIGN.md and .impeccable/design.json belong to the camera dashboard.

lamp.purpose: The judgement word only; 11rem kiosk, 8.5rem laptop, 5.5rem phone; steps down by word length instead of wrapping.

wordmark.purpose: Product name on the navy title bar.

readout.purpose: Live mismatch value beside its limit.

reason.purpose: The sentence explaining the current state; max 60ch, reserved 4.05em height.

body.purpose: Table cells, frame strip, empty wells.

note.purpose: Rule notes, history text, match note.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Lamp, ROI box, panes, strip and judgement cells switch in the same frame.

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: HMI key hover and press; removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: key-flash
motion.purpose: Visible press when a key is triggered from the keyboard.

motion.name: hold-to-exit
motion.purpose: Kiosk exit key fill while held; cancels on release.

motion.name: live-data
motion.purpose: Only the match bar, trends and clock move, at the data rate.

narrative.overview:
Vizion Motor reads like the operator panel of an industrial machine-vision sensor: a light grey panel, navy title bars, white image wells, and one judgement lamp. Every camera frame is an inspection of the servo arm against its master image, and the screen is arranged so the verdict, the evidence that decided it, and the score sit side by side. It is legible from across a desk: the lamp word is set as large as ANOMALY fits its column, the keys are 64px rectangles, and every number uses tabular figures.

The panel is flat and square. Depth comes only from navy keylines and the change from panel grey to white wells; there are no shadows, no radius, no blur. Colour is rationed: navy carries structure and ink, cyan marks what the inspection tool is looking at, and green and red appear only where a judgement is being shown. That rationing is what lets a trip read instantly: when the arm is grabbed, the lamp, the region box, both pane frames and the HELD FRAME stamp go red in the same frame, and nothing else on the screen is red to compete.

It behaves like hardware. State changes are instant; only live data (the match bar, the trends, the clock) moves. The kiosk view fits one 1920×1080 screen without scrolling.
keyCharacteristics: Light panel grey ground, navy title bars and ink, white image wells with 1px navy keylines.
Square corners everywhere (0px); flat, no shadows.
Green and red reserved for judgements; cyan for inspection overlays, selection and focus.
Barlow Condensed for the lamp, keys, field names and readouts; Barlow for sentences; tabular figures throughout.
Rectangular HMI keys that invert to navy when pressed.
Instant state changes; only live data moves.

rules.name: The Judgement-Only Rule
rules.body: Green and red appear only where a judgement is shown: the lamp, the region box and its tool tag, judgement cells and history chips, the match bar past its limit, and the anomaly evidence (held pane frames, HELD FRAME stamp, trend trip marks). Never as decoration, branding, or a generic success/error colour for UI chrome.

rules.name: The Navy-Below-Limit Rule
rules.body: A measurement is navy until it crosses its limit. The match bar fills navy and turns red only past the limit; it is never green, because a value is not a judgement.

rules.name: The Cyan-Looks Rule
rules.body: Cyan means "the tool is looking here": overlays, selection, focus, and what the camera saw. It never carries a verdict.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Condensed uppercase is the machine labelling and judging; regular sentence case is the machine explaining to a person. Sentences are never set in condensed caps, and labels are never set in sentence case.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every figure is tabular. Numbers that update at the frame rate must not shift their neighbours.

rules.name: The Reserved Slot Rule
rules.body: Anything that changes on a trip occupies a slot that already exists. The frame strip is always one line under the panes and becomes HELD FRAME in place; the reason keeps a reserved 4.05em height; the lamp word steps down a size instead of wrapping. Nothing moves when the station trips.

rules.name: The Keyline Rule
rules.body: Separation is drawn with a line, never cast with a shadow: 1px navy for wells and windows, 1px rule-grey inside tables, 2px navy for keys and the lamp bezel, 3px red for held panes.

dos: **Do** keep every corner square (0px) and every surface flat; separate with navy keylines.
**Do** reserve green and red for judgements and anomaly evidence, and keep measurements navy until they cross their limit.
**Do** use cyan only for what the inspection is looking at: ROI boxes at rest, the tool tag, the camera's trace, selection and focus.
**Do** switch state instantly; let only live data (bar, trends, clock) move. The only timed transitions are the 150ms key background/colour change and the 1000ms hold-to-exit fill.
**Do** reserve a slot for anything that changes on a trip, so the layout never shifts.
**Do** set labels in Barlow Condensed uppercase and sentences in Barlow sentence case, with tabular figures everywhere.
**Do** use dashed borders for not-yet or unavailable states and hatching for absence.
donts: **Don't** use KPI tiles or big-number cards for counts; counts are a ruled table row.
**Don't** add shadows, rounded corners, tonal gradients, or blur; the 45° hatching for absence is the only patterned fill.
**Don't** colour the match bar green; below the limit it is navy.
**Don't** let the lamp word wrap; step its size down instead.
**Don't** show a stale limit while the system is re-learning.
**Don't** animate state changes (no fades, slides or pulses on the lamp, box or panes).
